lines.speaker: Wei Ling
lines.text: Okay, everyone's here. This is the Nanyang Kopi and Toast launch check for Raffles Place. Four items today: the kiosk Kopi names, the morning seat crunch, the SFA food safety inspection, then the delivery platform commission squeeze.

lines.speaker: Wei Ling
lines.text: Mei, let's start with the kiosk. What did the trial show?

lines.speaker: Mei
lines.text: Yesterday's trial had 28 first-time users. Nineteen of them froze for over two minutes at Kopi O Kosong, Kopi C Siew Dai or Teh Halia.

lines.speaker: Mei
lines.text: Seventy-two percent never noticed the small language toggle in the corner.

lines.speaker: Arjun
lines.text: Renaming the buttons is not free. The kitchen docket prints the same name the customer sees, so the uncles would have to read the English name.

lines.speaker: Arjun
lines.text: When we tested that at Tampines, drink prep slowed by fifteen seconds a cup. And the fifteen-inch screen only fits twelve buttons per page.

lines.speaker: Wei Ling
lines.text: So what helps a first-timer without slowing the kitchen?

lines.speaker: Mei
lines.text: I can try a clearer drink step, but I don't know if it fits the twelve-button grid.

lines.speaker: Arjun
lines.text: I can check what fits tonight, but any label change needs a kitchen test before eight.

lines.speaker: Wei Ling
lines.text: Mei, can you file a ticket for the kiosk label experiment so it is tracked with the trial numbers?

lines.speaker: Mei
lines.text: Yes, I'll file it today with the nineteen out of twenty-eight numbers.

lines.speaker: Daniel
lines.text: Do we know if tourists or locals struggled more?

lines.speaker: Mei
lines.text: The trial sheet has that split, but I haven't looked at it since last week.

lines.speaker: Wei Ling
lines.text: Okay, that is the kiosk item. Let's move to the morning seat crunch.

lines.speaker: Wei Ling
lines.text: Our twenty-eight seats were jammed again this morning.

lines.speaker: Wei Ling
lines.text: Four laptop freelancers held our four 4-seater booths, that's sixteen seats, for two hours on a single two-dollar-twenty Kopi O.

lines.speaker: Wei Ling
lines.text: That is about four hundred and twenty dollars in lost breakfast sets. And Auntie Mary is still shaken after that guy in a suit yelled at her.

lines.speaker: Mei
lines.text: Sixty percent of our morning customers dine solo. They cannot carry a hot tray of runny eggs without a table.

lines.speaker: Arjun
lines.text: The twelve booth wall sockets and guest Wi-Fi run on a smart relay breaker in the back room. I can cut power, but that also hits paying customers.

lines.speaker: Wei Ling
lines.text: Who enforces any new seating rule if it cannot be Auntie Mary?

lines.speaker: Mei
lines.text: That is the hard part. If we ban tissue packets, a solo diner with a hot tray has nowhere to sit while the queue clears.

lines.speaker: Arjun
lines.text: I still have the numbered table pucks in the storeroom, but I don't know if handing them out after payment fixes the queue.

lines.speaker: Wei Ling
lines.text: How many solo diners actually need a table between eight and ten? Do we have that number?

lines.speaker: Mei
lines.text: Not per hour. The trial sheet has the split, but I would have to check it.

lines.speaker: Wei Ling
lines.text: Okay, let's not decide blind. Put the per-hour solo diner number on the list.

lines.speaker: Arjun
lines.text: I can pull the socket usage from the relay, but that won't tell us who is a camper.

lines.speaker: Wei Ling
lines.text: Fine, keep that open. Moving on to the SFA food safety inspection.

lines.speaker: Wei Ling
lines.text: Daniel, you saw the SFA notice.

lines.speaker: Daniel
lines.text: A customer reported suspected salmonella from our soft-boiled eggs during the trial, and SFA is inspecting our kitchen tomorrow at nine.

lines.speaker: Wei Ling
lines.text: The hospital lab test takes forty-eight hours. We have a pasteurized backup egg batch on standby, and it costs one hundred and eighty dollars a day.

lines.speaker: Arjun
lines.text: The sous-vide water bath holds eggs at sixty-three degrees, and the digital probe logs every fifteen minutes.

lines.speaker: Mei
lines.text: Pulling soft-boiled eggs off the menu breaks Set A, which is eighty percent of our morning orders. And holding above sixty-five degrees curdles the yolks.

lines.speaker: Wei Ling
lines.text: Both egg station staff are flat out during the eight o'clock rush.

lines.speaker: Daniel
lines.text: So who logs the water bath temperatures, and how do we reassure customers at the counter?

lines.speaker: Arjun
lines.text: I can export the sixty-three-degree water bath log from the tablet, but someone has to verify it before nine.

lines.speaker: Wei Ling
lines.text: And how are the batch certificates checked and signed off at close?

lines.speaker: Arjun
lines.text: That is still open. We haven't assigned who signs off the batch log at close.

lines.speaker: Wei Ling
lines.text: Okay, the SFA sign-off is not settled. Last item, the delivery platform commission squeeze.

lines.speaker: Wei Ling
lines.text: Daniel, where are we with GrabFood?

lines.speaker: Daniel
lines.text: GrabFood and Foodpanda raised our CBD breakfast commission to thirty-two percent, so we lose forty cents on every single ten-dollar set delivered.

lines.speaker: Daniel
lines.text: They will feature our five-set corporate bundle platter tomorrow for six hundred cash, or four-fifty plus twenty self-pickup vouchers from our storeroom.

lines.speaker: Mei
lines.text: Marking up single sets by thirty percent triggers GrabFood's price-parity penalty, and delivery drives half of our morning volume.

lines.speaker: Mei
lines.text: A five-set corporate platter avoids the single-item penalty, and a QR self-pickup flyer is ready too. I would need to test the prep flow at the counter.

lines.speaker: Wei Ling
lines.text: Single-set packaging and commissions eat forty cents a set, about eleven hundred a month in margin, and we only have seven hundred and fifty left in the launch budget.

lines.speaker: Arjun
lines.text: Our direct QR link has zero commission for self-pickup, so office runners at the counter will see the direct price.

lines.speaker: Daniel
lines.text: Which bundles stay on GrabFood, and how do we move single orders to QR self-pickup?

lines.speaker: Mei
lines.text: I can set up the five-set corporate platter and the self-pickup shelf, but we still have to choose the minimum order rule.

lines.speaker: Wei Ling
lines.text: Daniel, can you email GrabFood and confirm the five-set platter listing for tomorrow?

lines.speaker: Daniel
lines.text: Yes, I'll email GrabFood tonight and confirm the details.

lines.speaker: Wei Ling
lines.text: And I'll post the final plan in the team channel once we settle the delivery decision.

lines.speaker: Arjun
lines.text: We still haven't settled the single-set minimum, though.

lines.speaker: Wei Ling
lines.text: Right, keep the minimum open for now. That's everything.

lines.speaker: Wei Ling
lines.text: Thanks all, good meeting.
